_comment: Rule-based trump selection. PLAN.md §1.4 puts this in a file rather than in code: it is tiny, hand-tunable and reviewable in git. §3.1 says a ranked rule-based selector comes within ~0.7 points of a learned one, so this is meant to be nearly all of the available gain, not a placeholder.

trump_rank_weights._comment: Per card, for the suit being considered as trump. Follows trump power (J>9>A>K>Q>10>8>7>6) rather than card value: the Puur always wins a trick AND carries 20 points, while the 10 carries 10 points but loses to five other trumps.

trump_length_bonus._comment: Trump length is worth more than trump quality past a point — every spare trump is a ruff. Indexed by how many trumps are held.

side_suit_weights._comment: Cards outside the trump suit, when this suit is trump. An ace usually wins its trick; a king mostly does not unless protected.

side_void_bonus._comment: A void or singleton in a side suit is a ruffing opportunity, but only if trumps back it up. Scaled by trump count in code.

obenabe_weights._comment: High cards win. Aces dominate; the 8 is worth 8 points in a no-trump contract.

undenufe_weights._comment: Mirror image: the 6 is highest and worth 11 points, the ace is worthless.

no_trump_top_run_bonus._comment: In a no-trump contract, consecutive top cards in one suit cash immediately. Rewards A-K-Q or 6-7-8 held together.

baseline._comment: Score of an unremarkable hand. Contracts are compared on (score - baseline) * multiplier, because the multiplier scales the stakes for BOTH teams -- it multiplies your edge, not your points. A mediocre hand at x4 is a bad idea, not a good one.

shove_threshold._comment: Forehand shoves when the best available edge is below this. Shoving is valuable and PLAN.md §3.1 notes search-based selectors underperform largely because they never learn to do it.
